entries.originalText: “My Son, beware thou dispute not of high matters and of the hidden judgments of God; why this man is thus left, and that man is taken into so great favour; why also this man is so greatly afflicted, and that so highly exalted.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, beware of disputing about high matters and the hidden judgments of God: why one person is thus left and another taken into such great favor; why one is so greatly afflicted and another so highly exalted.

entries.originalText: These things pass all man’s power of judging, neither may any reasoning or disputation have power to search out the divine judgments.
entries.modernizedText: These things surpass all human power of judgment, and no reasoning or dispute can search out the divine judgments.

entries.originalText: When therefore the enemy suggesteth these things to thee, or when any curious people ask such questions, answer with that word of the Prophet, Just art Thou, O Lord, and true is Thy judgment,(1) and with this, The judgments of the Lord are true, and righteous altogether.(2) My judgments are to be feared, not to be disputed on, because they are incomprehensible to human understanding.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, when the enemy suggests these things to you, or curious people ask such questions, answer with the Prophet’s words, Just are You, O Lord, and true is Your judgment,(1) and with these: The judgments of the Lord are true, and righteous altogether.(2) My judgments are to be feared, not disputed, because they are beyond human understanding.

entries.originalText: “And be not given to inquire or dispute about the merits of the Saints, which is holier than another, or which is the greater in the Kingdom of Heaven.
entries.modernizedText: “Do not be given to asking or disputing about the merits of the Saints, which is holier than another, or which is greater in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.originalText: Such questions often beget useless strifes and contentions: they also nourish pride and vain glory, whence envyings and dissensions arise, while one man arrogantly endeavoureth to exalt one Saint and another another.
entries.modernizedText: Such questions often produce useless strife and contention; they also nourish pride and vain glory, from which envy and disagreements arise, while one person arrogantly tries to exalt one Saint and another exalts another.

entries.originalText: But to wish to know and search out such things bringeth no fruit, but it rather displeaseth the Saints; for I am not the God of confusion but of peace;(3) which peace consisteth more in true humility than in self-exaltation.
entries.modernizedText: But wishing to know and search out such things bears no fruit; instead it displeases the Saints, for I am not the God of confusion but of peace,(3) and that peace consists more in true humility than in self-exaltation.

entries.originalText: “Some are drawn by zeal of love to greater affection to these Saints or those; but this is human affection rather than divine.
entries.modernizedText: “Some are drawn by zeal of love to greater affection for certain Saints; but this is human rather than divine affection.

entries.originalText: I am He Who made all the Saints: I gave them grace, I brought them glory; I know the merits of every one; I prevented them with the blessings of My goodness.(4) I foreknew my beloved ones from everlasting, I chose them out of the world;(5) they did not choose Me.
entries.modernizedText: I am He who made all the Saints: I gave them grace, I brought them glory, I know the merits of each one, and I went before them with the blessings of My goodness.(4) I knew My beloved ones from eternity and chose them out of the world;(5) they did not choose Me.

entries.originalText: I called them by My grace, drew them by My mercy, led them on through sundry temptations.
entries.modernizedText: I called them by My grace, drew them by My mercy, and led them through various temptations.

entries.originalText: I poured mighty consolations upon them, I gave them perseverance, I crowned their patience.
entries.modernizedText: I poured mighty consolations upon them, gave them perseverance, and crowned their patience.

entries.originalText: “I acknowledge the first and the last; I embrace all with inestimable love.
entries.modernizedText: “I acknowledge the first and the last; I embrace all with immeasurable love.

entries.originalText: I am to be praised in all My Saints; I am to be blessed above all things, and to be honoured in every one whom I have so gloriously exalted and predestined, without any preceding merits of their own.
entries.modernizedText: I am to be praised in all My Saints; I am to be blessed above all things and honored in each one whom I have so gloriously exalted and predestined, without any preceding merits of their own.

entries.originalText: He therefore that shall despise one of the least of these My people, honoureth not the great; because I made both small and great.(6) And he who speaketh against any of My Saints speaketh against Me, and against all others in the Kingdom of Heaven.”
entries.modernizedText: Therefore whoever despises one of the least of these My people does not honor the great, because I made both small and great.(6) And whoever speaks against any of My Saints speaks against Me and against all the others in the Kingdom of Heaven.”

entries.originalText: They are all one through the bond of charity; they think the same thing, will the same thing, and all are united in love one to another.
entries.modernizedText: They are all one through the bond of charity; they think the same thing, will the same thing, and are all united in love to one another.

entries.originalText: “But yet (which is far better) they love Me above themselves and their own merits.
entries.modernizedText: “But yet, what is far better, they love Me above themselves and their own merits.

entries.originalText: For being caught up above themselves, and drawn beyond self-love, they go all straightforward to the love of Me, and they rest in Me in perfect enjoyment.
entries.modernizedText: For being caught up above themselves and drawn beyond self-love, they go straight toward love of Me and rest in Me in perfect enjoyment.

entries.originalText: There is nothing which can turn them away or press them down; for being full of Eternal Truth, they burn with the fire of inextinguishable charity.
entries.modernizedText: Nothing can turn them away or press them down; for being full of Eternal Truth, they burn with the fire of unquenchable charity.

entries.originalText: Therefore let all carnal and natural men hold their peace concerning the state of the Saints, for they know nothing save to love their own personal enjoyment.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore let all carnal and natural people be silent concerning the state of the Saints, for they know only how to love their own personal enjoyment.

entries.originalText: They take away and add according to their own inclination, not as it pleaseth the Eternal Truth.
entries.modernizedText: They take away and add according to their own inclination, not as pleases the Eternal Truth.

entries.originalText: “In many men this is ignorance, chiefly is it so in those who, being little enlightened, rarely learn to love any one with perfect spiritual love.
entries.modernizedText: “In many people this is ignorance, especially in those who, being little enlightened, rarely learn to love anyone with perfect spiritual love.

entries.originalText: They are still much drawn by natural affection and human friendship to these or to those: and as they reckon of themselves in lower matters, so also do they frame imaginations of things heavenly.
entries.modernizedText: They are still greatly drawn by natural affection and human friendship to one or another; and as they judge themselves in lower matters, so they form imaginations of heavenly things.

entries.originalText: But there is an immeasurable difference between those things which they imperfectly imagine, and these things which enlightened men behold through supernatural revelation.
entries.modernizedText: But there is an immeasurable difference between what they imperfectly imagine and what enlightened people behold through supernatural revelation.

entries.originalText: “Take heed, therefore, My son, that thou treat not curiously those things which surpass thy knowledge, but rather make this thy business and give attention to it, namely, that thou seek to be found, even though it be the least, in the Kingdom of God.
entries.modernizedText: “Take care, therefore, My son, not to pry into things that surpass your knowledge, but make it your business and give attention to this: seek to be found, even as the least, in the Kingdom of God.

entries.originalText: And even if any one should know who were holier than others, or who were held greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven; what should that knowledge profit him, unless through this knowledge he should humble himself before Me, and should rise up to give greater praise unto My name?
entries.modernizedText: And even if someone knew who was holier than others or who was held greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, what would that knowledge profit him unless through it he humbled himself before Me and rose to give greater praise to My name?

entries.originalText: He who considereth how great are his own sins, how small his virtues, and how far he is removed from the perfection of the Saints, doeth far more acceptably in the sight of God, than he who disputeth about their greatness or littleness.
entries.modernizedText: Whoever considers how great his own sins are, how small his virtues, and how far he is from the perfection of the Saints acts far more acceptably in God’s sight than one who disputes about their greatness or smallness.

entries.originalText: “They are altogether well content, if men would learn to be content, and to refrain from vain babbling.
entries.modernizedText: “They are altogether content, if only people would learn to be content and refrain from vain babbling.

entries.originalText: They glory not of their own merits, seeing they ascribe no good unto themselves, but all unto Me, seeing that I of my infinite charity have given them all things.
entries.modernizedText: They do not glory in their own merits, since they ascribe no good to themselves but all to Me, because I have given them all things out of My infinite charity.

entries.originalText: They are filled with so great love of the Divinity, and with such overflowing joy, that no glory is lacking to them, neither can any felicity be lacking.
entries.modernizedText: They are filled with such great love of the Divinity and such overflowing joy that no glory is lacking to them, nor can any happiness be lacking.

entries.originalText: All the Saints, the higher they are exalted in glory, the humbler are they in themselves, and the nearer and dearer are they unto Me.
entries.modernizedText: The higher all the Saints are exalted in glory, the humbler they are in themselves, and the nearer and dearer they are to Me.

entries.originalText: And so thou hast it written that they cast their crowns before God and fell on their faces before the Lamb, and worshipped Him that liveth for ever and ever.(7)
entries.modernizedText: And so you have it written that they cast their crowns before God and fell on their faces before the Lamb, and worshiped Him who lives forever and ever.(7)

entries.originalText: “Many ask who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, who know not whether they shall be worthy to be counted among the least.
entries.modernizedText: “Many ask who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven who do not know whether they will be worthy to be counted among the least.

entries.originalText: It is a great thing to be even the least in Heaven, where all are great, because all shall be called, and shall be, the sons of God.
entries.modernizedText: It is a great thing to be even the least in Heaven, where all are great, because all will be called, and will be, the children of God.

entries.originalText: A little one shall become a thousand, but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed.
entries.modernizedText: A little one shall become a thousand, but the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed.

entries.originalText: For when the disciples asked who should be the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, they received no other answer than this, Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
entries.modernizedText: For when the disciples asked who would be greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, they received no other answer than this: Unless you are converted and become as little children, you shall not enter the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.originalText: But whosoever shall humble himself as this little child, the same shall be greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.”(8)
entries.modernizedText: But whoever humbles himself as this little child shall be greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.”(8)

entries.originalText: Woe unto them who disdain to humble themselves willingly with the little children; for the low gate of the kingdom of Heaven will not suffer them to enter in.
entries.modernizedText: Woe to those who refuse to humble themselves willingly with little children, for the low gate of the Kingdom of Heaven will not allow them to enter.

entries.originalText: Woe also to them who are rich, who have their consolation here;(9) because whilst the poor enter into the kingdom of God, they shall stand lamenting without.
entries.modernizedText: Woe also to those who are rich, who have their consolation here;(9) because while the poor enter the kingdom of God, they will stand lamenting outside.

entries.originalText: Rejoice ye humble, and exult ye poor, for yours is the kingdom of God if only ye walk in the truth.
entries.modernizedText: Rejoice, you humble, and exult, you poor, for yours is the kingdom of God if only you walk in the truth.
